name: Imperial City of Huế
summary: The walled palace city of the Nguyễn emperors, Vietnam's last dynasty, inside the great citadel on the Perfume River.

eras.title: A new capital
eras.text: Gia Long, the first Nguyễn emperor, began building a vast square citadel in 1805, with an imperial city and a forbidden purple city at its heart.

eras.title: The Meridian Gate
eras.text: Emperor Minh Mạng built the Meridian Gate, Ngọ Môn, as the ceremonial entrance to the Imperial City, topped by the Pavilion of the Five Phoenixes.

eras.title: The last enthronement
eras.text: In 1926 Bảo Đại was enthroned in the Hall of Supreme Harmony. Under French rule, the emperors kept their ceremonies but had little real power.

eras.title: The end of the monarchy
eras.text: On 30 August 1945, Bảo Đại read his abdication at the Meridian Gate and handed the imperial seal and sword to the new revolutionary government.

eras.title: Destruction
eras.text: During the Tết Offensive of 1968, the citadel was the scene of weeks of street fighting. Most of the buildings of the Forbidden Purple City were destroyed.

eras.label: 1993 – today
eras.title: World Heritage and restoration
eras.text: In 1993 Huế became Vietnam's first World Heritage Site. Palaces, gates and galleries have been restored one by one since.

story.title: The last emperor's farewell
story.narration: In August 1945, as the August Revolution swept the country, Emperor Bảo Đại decided to give up the throne. On 30 August, at the Meridian Gate, he read his abdication before a large crowd. He is remembered for saying that he would rather be a citizen of an independent country than the king of an enslaved one. He handed the golden seal and the sword of the dynasty to representatives of the new government. The 143 years of the Nguyễn dynasty, and two thousand years of monarchy in Vietnam, came to an end.

story.title: The nine dynastic urns
story.narration: In front of the Thế Miếu, the temple of the Nguyễn emperors, stand nine huge bronze urns, cast under Emperor Minh Mạng in the 1830s. Each is named after an emperor, and their sides are decorated with images of Vietnam: its mountains, rivers, seas, animals, plants and weapons. Together they form a kind of encyclopedia of the country in bronze, meant to show that the dynasty would last as long as the land itself.

story.title: Music of the court
story.narration: Nhã nhạc, 'elegant music', was played at court ceremonies, coronations and offerings to Heaven. Orchestras of drums, flutes, string instruments and gongs accompanied ritual dances. When the monarchy ended, the musicians scattered and the music almost disappeared. In 2003 UNESCO listed it as heritage of humanity, and today it is performed again in the restored theatre of the Imperial City.

story.title: From above: the Imperial City

video.file: Aerial view hoang thanh hue video.webm
video.alt: Drone video over the Imperial City of Huế, showing gates, courtyards and lawns along its central axis

story.narration: This drone film, made in September 2024, flies over the Imperial City of Huế. From above you can see how carefully it was planned: square walls and moats, with the most important gates, courtyards and halls lined up along one central axis. The Nguyễn emperors began building it in 1804. The whole citadel faces the Perfume River and Ngự Bình hill, a position chosen by geomancy. The video has no sound.

guide.price: Ticket to the Imperial City; combined tickets also cover the royal tombs.

hours.notes: Approximate. On some evenings the Imperial City stays open late.

do: Cover your shoulders and knees, and take off your hat inside the halls.
Walk quietly, and let worshippers go first.
Allow at least half a day; the site is large.
See the royal tombs of Minh Mạng, Tự Đức and Khải Định outside the city.
dont: Climb on walls, towers or statues.
Photograph people who are praying without asking.
Sit on the thrones or cross the ropes.

tips.title: Huế food
tips.text: Bún bò Huế, bánh bèo (small steamed rice cakes) and chè (sweet soups) by the river.

tips.title: Getting there
tips.text: Phú Bài airport is 15 km away; trains run on the North–South line.

tips.title: Nearby
tips.text: Thiên Mụ Pagoda, a boat trip on the Perfume River, and Đông Ba market.
